result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md: the send-once notification ledger, the transactional/marketing send API, the Telegram rate-limit/backoff wrapper, and the first scheduled-job-runner mechanism in this codebase.

SCHEMA CHANGE NEEDED -- YES, flagged for DATA-DESIGNER (Sec1), not designed here: a new `notification_ledger`-shaped table keyed UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), FK to registrations (onDelete restrict), a closed 'kind' value set (Release 1 needs exactly 6: admission_result/waitlist_promotion/reminder_24h/reminder_3h/feedback_request/event_cancelled; S10 names 2 future marketing kinds), and a caller-supplied 'sent at' timestamp (never defaultNow(), per decisions/0006). text-vs-pgEnum for 'kind' is left as DATA-DESIGNER's own call, framed against REQ-011's own stated tradeoff for admission/eventStatus.

CRUX (AC1) RESOLVED (Sec3.1/3.2): sendLedgeredNotification inserts the ledger row FIRST (a single, already-atomic INSERT; unique-violation on retry = normal 'skipped-already-sent' outcome, never an error) and only THEN calls the rate-limited Telegram send. This makes duplicate sends structurally impossible (a second run's insert fails, so it never re-sends) at the cost of an explicitly accepted, named risk: if the process crashes between the ledger insert committing and the Telegram call actually completing, the message can be silently, permanently NOT delivered -- stated precisely as the deliberate trade-off (under-send, never over-send) since Telegram's API offers no cross-system transactional guarantee. The reverse ordering (send-then-insert) is explicitly rejected in the doc because it can double-send on a crash between the two. Sec3.3 states AC1 requires a genuine two-process test (kill after the stubbed send call has actually returned in run 1), named explicitly for TEST-DESIGNER.

STAFF.TS SCOPING RESOLVED (Sec0.1): migrating apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts (ISS-0020) onto this ledger is OUT OF SCOPE for REQ-025 -- staff.ts's assignment/removal notifications are synchronous, request-scoped, one-off sends with no restart/retry surface (S9 does not apply, per staff.ts's own header comment), and structurally have no Registration row to key a (registration_id, kind) ledger entry on at all (they're keyed on event_id/user_id via EventStaff). ISS-0020's own narrow, already-filed fix (add a blocked projection + guard, mirroring REQ-023's existing pattern) is untouched and remains the correct fix, left for its own separate run.

WITHDRAW.TS MIGRATION STATED PRECISELY (Sec4): sendPromotionNotification's `ctx: Context` param is removed and replaced by an injected `sender: NotificationSender`; its `withdrawnRegistrationId` param is renamed to `promotedRegistrationId` and its value changes from the withdrawn row's id to `outcome.promotion.registrationId` (the promoted row's own id, already on PromotionOutcome per REQ-023 Sec3 step 7) -- this is the exact ledger key. The function's body becomes one call to the new shared sendLedgeredNotification with kind:'waitlist_promotion', classification:'transactional'. makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler gains a `sender` parameter; index.ts constructs one process-wide NotificationSender and threads it through. This explicitly REPLACES REQ-023 Sec5's implicit DB-state-only at-most-once argument (named there as this exact deferral) rather than leaving it alongside the new ledger.

Other design elements: NotificationKind/SendClassification closed unions with classification carrying no default (AC5, structural -- no `?`, no default in the interface); sequencing table where blocked-check (AC4) runs unconditionally before the classification/broadcastOptIn branch (AC3); domain/user.ts's UserForNotification gains broadcastOptIn (type-only addition, column already exists); scheduler/rateLimiter.ts's NotificationSender implementation (429 -> GrammyError.error_code===429 -> wait retry_after (or 1000ms default) -> retry, doubling up to 30000ms cap, 5 attempts, AC6); scheduler/runner.ts's startScheduledJobs (first scheduling infra in this codebase -- setInterval-based, immediate-first-run, per-job overlap guard, failure isolation) wired in index.ts with an EMPTY job list -- REQ-025 ships the mechanism only, REQ-026 supplies actual T-24h/T-3h job bodies; AC1 is verified directly against sendLedgeredNotification with a literal kind:'reminder_24h' argument, not a real job. Every AC mapped to a concrete design element in Sec9's table. 3 open questions stated explicitly (Sec8): ledger column/type detail (DATA-DESIGNER's), whether a failed-after-ledger-commit send should ever be retried by a later tick (left to REQ-026), and staff.ts/ISS-0020 sequencing relative to this run (ORCH's call, not a design question).
result.next_action: Route to DATA-DESIGNER for the notification_ledger schema design (Sec1 of docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md), then to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) once the schema artefact exists.
